### Context

Opening `/widgets/` locally showed page not found (404). Removing the final slash before the address check made it load, which confirmed the cause. A search of earlier reports found no match, and no test was blocked.

### What is broken

Opening `/widgets/` shows page not found (404) instead of the widgets page. `/widgets` without the final slash works.

### Why it is broken

The part that matches web addresses to pages compares them character for character, so `/widgets/` never equals `/widgets`. When the final slash was removed before the check, the same request loaded the page successfully (200, the normal success response).

### How to fix it

Remove a final slash from the address before it is compared, so both forms open the widgets page. The change touches one comparison, plus a test that repeats the failing request to check that it stays fixed. Choose hotfix, because the change is small, its effect is fully known, and it passed every safety check.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and moves two from fails to holds: the sectioned headings put the reporter's browser-and-version request inside a What happens next section, and the report body now translates shorthand on first use ("page not found (404)", "200, the normal success response", "browser settings that had no saved preferences", "safety check") where Before left "falsification test", "hypothesis", "tracked baseline", "delta at checkpoint 2" and "predicates" unexplained and wrapped the only citation inside a mid-claim parenthetical. The gate stays at roughly 160 words with a three-line Context, the menu, [recommended] row and eligibility line are untouched, both checkpoints end at their envelope, and the draft never claims a push. Two small tightenings would make the contract more robust without costing anything: in the gate's How to fix it, the person choosing hotfix will open the comparison next, so a trailing `(src/router.ts:88)` after "touches one comparison" is a citation the reader's next action actually requires and the wording should say so explicitly rather than leaving it to the model to omit; and the Context phrase "no test was blocked" is everyday but vague - the wording should direct the model to state the baseline outcome plainly (e.g. "the existing checks all passed before and after") so readers are not left guessing what was checked.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves plain-reader and draft-asks-reporter to holds: it translates 404/200, 'falsification test', 'normalization' and 'clean profiles' into everyday descriptions, names the router by its role, and gives the reporter draft the fixed headings with the browser/version request in What happens next. It keeps every fact Before kept. Two things to tighten so the gate stays maximally useful without weakening any fact: first, How to fix it gives the literal fix but drops the one citation the hotfix reader actually needs to open — append `(src/router.ts:88)` after the comparison claim, since the next action requires finding that line; second, the menu echo flipped row 3 from `[ ]` to `[x]`, which pre-selects the pick before the human chooses — keep all boxes unchecked and let `[recommended]` carry the suggestion. Optionally rename or soften the Why it is broken section for negative verdicts (e.g. 'Why we could not confirm it') so the heading does not assert a breakage the verdict denies.
